result.topic_en: Euler decomposes the force acting at a point of a flexible or elastic thread into a tangential force T and a normal force V applied at distance v, notes that V vanishes for a perfectly flexible thread, and states that for an elastic thread the curvature requires a moment Vv determined by the nature of the elastic material.

items.quote: si filum omni elasticitate careat, seu perfecte sit flexile, tum vim normalem V euanescere debere, neque propterea interuallum $v$ in calculum ingredi
items.english: If the thread lacks all elasticity, i.e. is perfectly flexible, then the normal force V must vanish, and therefore the interval v does not enter the calculation.

items.quote: si filum fuerit elasticum, tum curuatura in puncto $m$, quae ex angulo elementari $Tmt$ aestimatur, certum virium momentum postulabit, ex indole elateris definiendum, cui aequale esse debet momentum vis normalis VP, quod est $Vv$
items.english: If the thread is elastic, then the curvature at point m, estimated from the elementary angle Tmt, will require a certain moment of forces, to be defined from the nature of the spring, to which the moment of the normal force VP, namely Vv, must be equal.

items.quote: transferamus ea secundum principia differentialium ad punctum proximum $m$
items.english: Let us transfer these, according to the principles of differentials, to the next point m.
